SECURITY / RESPONSIBLE REPORTING

Preserve the evidence.
Protect the people.

A private route for vulnerabilities, with clear boundaries for reports and application-owned evidence.

Please report suspected package vulnerabilities privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting form. A GitHub account is required. Do not open a public issue containing an exploit, credential, private trace or customer data. Use a synthetic reproduction and include package/Python/OS versions, impact and reproduction steps. Do not send working production credentials.

The latest stable release is the primary maintenance target. Version 1 core and schema compatibility are documented; no response deadline or long-term support period is promised. Security fixes and breaking changes will be stated in release notes. Research interfaces can evolve under their declared scope.

Default HTML reports omit arbitrary captured fields. They retain timing, counts and relationships and do not guarantee anonymity. --include-details explicitly includes the entire captured trace as escaped text. Keep those reports private when the trace is private. The offline renderer makes no network calls and does not execute verifiers, replay or application writes.

The framework does not authenticate your readback source or validate that a provider's metadata is true. Application-owned adapters must establish source trust and domain semantics. Sharing a report does not replace preserving the original trace and source evidence.
